title: spec review: C-O4 v3: `orchestrator serve` — bearer-authed HTTP API over goals (spec round 3 after T-0143; supersedes T-0142)
spec:
Why: the kgpt `modules/orchestrator` (Phase C, kgpt side) forwards start_goal/goal_status/list_goals/cancel_goal to a per-user endpoint; this is that endpoint, running in the executor container on the home network. Spec round 3 folds in spec reviews T-0140 and T-0143. Scope is 6 files by Planner decision: the requester field belongs in goals.py with its record, and README waits for the C-O5 runbook.

goals.py (small, additive): start(repo_path, goal_text, account_id="A", reinstall=False, requester=None) stores `requester` (string or None) on the goals.json record; _status_entry()/status()/list_goals() return it. Nothing else in goals.py changes. tests/test_goals.py: one test that start() with requester="alice" records it and status() returns it.

serve.py with starlette (import from the mcp dependency tree; if starlette or uvicorn is not importable, exit at startup with one line; do not add a dependency). serve.py does `from . import goals` and calls goals.start / goals.list_goals / goals.status / goals.stop through the module attribute, never `from .goals import start`, so tests can patch orchestrator.goals.* (T-0143 risk 2). All route handlers are plain `def` (not async) so starlette runs them in its threadpool: goals.start, git clone and goals.stop block for seconds and must not stall /healthz or other requests. Every response entry that describes a goal carries "repo": <slug> (the repos.toml key the caller used), added by serve.py on top of what goals.* returns, so multi-repo listings map back to slugs (T-0143 risk 3). Routes:
- GET /healthz (no auth) → 200 {"status": "ok"}.
- POST /goals body {repo, goal, requester?, account?}: 400 {"reason": ...} when repo or goal is missing, goal is empty/whitespace, or requester is present and not a string, or account is present and not a string (T-0143 risk 4; untrusted input is validated, never passed through); resolve slug via .orchestrator/repos.toml (slug → {path, git_url}); 404 {"reason": "unknown repo"} for an unknown slug; when path is missing and git_url is set, clone under a per-slug lock: fcntl flock on <ORCH_WORK>/.locks/<slug>.lock (mkdir -p; mirror goals.py's _with_goals_lock pattern), re-check that path is still missing inside the lock, then `git clone <git_url> <ORCH_WORK>/<slug>` as an argv list (ORCH_WORK env, default /work); clone failure → 502 {"reason": "clone failed", "detail": stderr[-500:]} (T-0143 risk 1); BEFORE calling start, call goals.list_goals(path) and if any record has record_status == "running" and planner_alive is True → 409 {"reason": "goal already running", "goal_id": <id>}; then goals.start(path, goal, account_id=body.get("account", "A"), requester=body.get("requester")); launched true → 201 {goal_id, repo: slug, status: "running", requester}; launched false → 422 {"reason": r["reason"]} (covers every precheck refusal); never a 500 for an expected refusal.
- GET /goals[?repo=slug] → 200 list: goals.list_goals(path) per configured repo (all repos when no filter; 404 unknown slug), each entry with "repo": slug.
- GET /goals/{repo}/{goal_id} → 200 goals.status(path, goal_id) entry with "repo": slug; 404 when the repo or goal is unknown.
- POST /goals/{repo}/{goal_id}/cancel → goals.stop(path, goal_id); {"error": "unknown goal"} → 404; else 200 {goal_id, repo: slug, status: "stopped"}.
Auth: every route except /healthz requires `Authorization: Bearer <ORCH_SERVICE_TOKEN>` (env; the server refuses to start with one line and non-zero exit when unset), compared with hmac.compare_digest; 401 {"reason": "unauthorized"} otherwise. The token is never stored, logged or echoed; access log lines contain method, path, status only.
cli.py: `serve [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8090]` runs uvicorn with the app. `.orchestrator/repos.toml.example` with one commented entry showing slug, path, git_url.

Tests tests/test_serve.py with starlette's TestClient and orchestrator.goals.start/list_goals/status/stop patched via unittest.mock.patch (no real git, no Popen): healthz_no_auth, rejects_missing_or_wrong_bearer, unknown_repo_404, empty_goal_400, bad_requester_type_400, start_returns_goal_id_and_requester (201; start called with requester and account kwargs; response repo == slug), start_refusal_422, second_start_409_while_running (list_goals returns a running+alive record → 409 and start NOT called), list_entries_carry_slug, clone_runs_under_lock_once (path missing + git_url set; subprocess.run patched: called once with an argv list starting ["git", "clone", ...]; lock file created under ORCH_WORK/.locks), cancel_marks_stopped, cancel_unknown_404, handlers_are_sync (no route endpoint is a coroutine function), serve_imports_goals_as_module (assert serve.goals is orchestrator.goals). No new dependency; finish with summary, files changed, failures-only test output; commit on the task branch when green.
acceptance: tests/test_serve.py has the fourteen named tests, green; tests/test_goals.py gains the requester test, green
goals.start accepts requester and status()/list_goals() return it; no other goals.py change (diff)

serve.py calls goals.* through the module attribute; every handler is a plain def; every start() refusal maps to 422; 409 comes from list_goals; every goal entry in a response carries repo = slug; requester/account are validated as strings or 400
First-use clone runs under a per-slug flock with a re-check inside the lock, as an argv list, once (test)
`uv run orchestrator serve` without ORCH_SERVICE_TOKEN exits non-zero with one line; no route logs, stores or echoes the bearer
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency; only the six scoped files change; committed on the task branch
